CSTEP Training · for the CSTEP Admin

Set up Travel Claims for your team

Before anyone files a request, four things have to exist: the projects requests are debited to, the vendors CSTEP pays, the employees who travel and claim — each mapped to an Approver, Official and Finance user — and the numbering every reference starts from.

Part 1 of 4

Projects

Every request is debited to a project. Add each one with its Tally cost centre.

  1. 1Open Project Master
  2. 2Add a project: code, Tally Project CC, name
  3. 3Many projects at once: Import
ProjectsStep 1 of 3 · Open Project Master

Travel Claims → Project Master

Open Travel Claims → Project Master. It lists every project a request can be debited to, with its Tally Project CC and status.

Only a CSTEP Admin sees Add project and Import. A Finance user can open the list to read it.

Travel Claims → Project MasterClick Add project
ProjectsStep 2 of 3 · Add a project

Start with the project code

Click Add project. Enter the Project code — your own code, e.g. PRJ-SOLAR. It can't be changed once saved: requests keep it on record.

Project code and Project name are required; everything else can follow.

ProjectsStep 2 of 3 · Add a project

Tally Project CC and the project name

Enter the Tally Project CC — the cost-centre code the Tally export writes against every voucher for this project.

Enter the Project name requesters pick from on every form. Leave Active ticked so it is offered on the request forms.

Code · Tally CC · nameAdd project
ProjectsStep 2 of 3 · Add a project

Saved — and on every request form

Click Add project to save. The project joins the list — here PRJ-HYDRO — and is offered at once on the Tour Proposal, Event Request, Local Travel Claim and Expense Claim.

Edit renames it, changes its cost centre or deactivates it. The code itself stays.

ProjectsStep 3 of 3 · Many projects at once

Import with the template

Import takes an Excel sheet: download the Excel template, fill one project per row (up to 500), Preview import, then commit.

Project Code is the key — a code that already exists updates that project, a new code adds one. Or edit an Export Excel and import it back.

Import → Excel templateFill · Preview · commit
Part 2 of 4

Vendors

Vendors are who CSTEP pays for arranged services. Each gets a CSTEPVEN code.

  1. 1Open Vendor Master
  2. 2Add a vendor: name, type, contact, GSTIN
  3. 3Vendor types
  4. 4Many vendors at once: Import
VendorsStep 1 of 3 · Open Vendor Master

Travel Claims → Vendor Master

Open Travel Claims → Vendor Master. Vendors are who CSTEP pays for the services an Official arranges — airlines, hotels, cabs, venues.

Each vendor has a CSTEPVEN code. Admin and Finance see the list; only the CSTEP Admin adds or edits.

Travel Claims → Vendor MasterClick Add vendor
VendorsStep 2 of 3 · Add a vendor

Name and type

Click Add vendor. The Vendor code is assigned when you save — you never type it.

Enter the Vendor name — it is also the vendor's ledger name in the Tally export — and pick the Vendor type.

VendorsStep 2 of 3 · Add a vendor

Vendor types — the list the dropdown offers

Manage (beside the type, or Manage types on the list) opens the vendor types: add one, rename one, or deactivate one. A type in use can be deactivated, not deleted.

The type decides the expense ledger the Tally export posts the vendor's lines to.

VendorsStep 2 of 3 · Add a vendor

Contact details and GSTIN

Add the contact details — mobile, email, city — and the GSTIN if the vendor has one. It is checked for format as you type.

Then click Add vendor.

Name + typeContact + GSTINAdd vendor
VendorsStep 2 of 3 · Add a vendor

Saved with its CSTEPVEN code

The confirmation names the code it issued — here CSTEPVEN0025 — and the vendor joins the list.

Vendor codes come from a continuous series; you can set where it continues from under Numbering (the last part of this deck).

VendorsStep 3 of 3 · Many vendors at once

Import with the vendor template

Import takes the vendor template: one vendor per row, up to 500. Leave Vendor Code blank to add a vendor; a code that matches updates that vendor.

Preview import shows every row and any problem before anything is saved; then commit.

Import → Excel templateFill · Preview · commit
Part 3 of 4

Employees

Each employee who files or travels is a traveller, keyed by their Employee ID — and mapped to who approves, arranges and reimburses.

  1. 1Open Travellers
  2. 2Add an employee: name, Employee ID, work email
  3. 3Map Approver, Official user, Finance user
  4. 4Many employees at once: Bulk Import
EmployeesStep 1 of 4 · Open Travellers

Your profile → Travellers

Open your profile → Travellers. Every employee who files a request or travels is listed here with their Traveller ID.

Add Traveller adds one person; Bulk Import adds many.

Profile → TravellersAdd Traveller
EmployeesStep 2 of 4 · Add an employee

Name as on their ID

Click Add Traveller. Enter the first and last name as on their ID.

Passport and the other travel documents are optional here — the employee can add them to their own profile later.

EmployeesStep 2 of 4 · Add an employee

Employee ID and work email

Under Organisation, the Employee ID is required in CSTEP — it becomes the person's Traveller ID on every request.

Under Contact, enter their official Work Email. It links the profile to their login, so they can claim it and file their own requests.

Employee ID (required)Work emailAdd traveller
EmployeesStep 2 of 4 · Add an employee

Saved — with their Traveller ID

Click Add traveller. The employee appears in the list with their Traveller ID — here NWR-1009, the Employee ID you entered.

EmployeesStep 3 of 4 · Map the employee

A new employee is not mapped yet

Scroll the list to the right: every traveller has an Approver, an Official user and a Finance user. A new employee starts as Not set — their requests have nowhere to go until you map them.

Only the CSTEP Admin sees and sets these three columns.

EmployeesStep 3 of 4 · Map the employee

Approver, Official user, Finance user

Pick each one from its dropdown — it saves as you choose.

The Approver sanctions or returns their requests, the Official user arranges their tour services, the Finance user reimburses them.

ApproverOfficial userFinance user
EmployeesStep 4 of 4 · Many employees at once

Bulk Import

For many employees: Bulk Import → download the CSV or Excel template → fill one row per employee, Employee ID included → Preview Import → import.

Up to 500 rows at a time. Map each imported employee's Approver, Official and Finance user in the list afterwards.

TemplateOne row per employeePreview · import
Part 4 of 4

Numbering

Set where every reference series starts — once, before the first request.

  1. 1Financial-year series: TIN, LTC, EXP, EVR
  2. 2Set a start — numbers only move forward
  3. 3Continuous series: vendor code, Tally voucher
  4. 4Recent changes
NumberingStep 1 of 4 · Open Numbering

Travel Claims → Numbering

Open Travel Claims → Numbering (CSTEP Admin only). It shows the next number each reference series will issue.

Financial-year series — Tour TIN, Local Travel (LTC), Expense (EXP) and Event (EVR) — restart at 1 every 1 April. Each row shows this year's next number and next year's start.

NumberingStep 2 of 4 · Set a start

Choose the year, type the start

To carry on from your old numbering, pick This year or Next year, type the start, then click Set start.

Here next year's Tour TIN will start at 101.

This year / Next yearType the startSet start
NumberingStep 2 of 4 · Set a start

Confirm — numbers only move forward

You are asked to confirm in plain words: Raise Tour TIN for FY 2027–28 from 1 to 101? Numbers 1–100 will never be issued, and this can't be lowered again.

A lower number is refused; the same number changes nothing.

NumberingStep 2 of 4 · Set a start

Done

The row now shows next year's start — 101 — and the next Tour TIN that year will be 0101/MMYY.

NumberingStep 3 of 4 · Continuous series

Vendor code and Tally voucher never restart

Continuous series never restart: the Vendor code (CSTEPVEN…) and the Tally voucher — the voucher number the Tally export writes.

Same rule: set a start, and numbers only move forward.

NumberingStep 4 of 4 · Recent changes

Every change is recorded

Recent changes lists every start that moved a series — when, which series and year, from what to what, and who made the change.
